inputs.text: President John Mahama is directly linking the nation's foundational policies to its legal frameworks, cultural ethos, and collective societal agreement, while stressing his dedication to upholding the rule of law amid these increasingly complex global human rights discussions. For those of us fighting for social justice, this is a clear signal that we must demand institutional reforms to dismantle historical inequalities, prioritize labor rights, and defend vulnerable groups from the discrimination built into cultural norms. He stated, “I took an oath to uphold [...] This moment demands we push harder against the structural barriers that have long protected the privileged at the expense of marginalized communities, because without bold changes rooted in equity, these pledges will only reinforce the status quo.
